topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer therapies and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated toxicities and multidrug resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic vulnerabilities of cancer cells, such as hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on small-molecule inhibitors designed to target hyperactive oncogenic kinases and the molecular pathways leading to drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the use of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to specifically target surface antigens on tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell redirection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the principles of antitumor immunity and therapies that stimulate or engineer T cells, including checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Challenges, future directions, and clinical dilemmas in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess historical progress and future paradigms in cancer management, highlighting ongoing challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, prevention, and clinical trial dilemmas.
